statement: For a finite graph with a fixed boundary identification xi and random-cluster weight p^|omega|(1-p)^(|E|-|omega|)q^k_xi(omega), where 0<p<1 and q>0, the conditional probability an edge e is open given every other edge equals p if its endpoints are already connected modulo xi, and p/(p+q(1-p)) otherwise.

source.description: Direct ratio of the two finite random-cluster configuration weights; external definition citation to be recovered.

proof: If the endpoints are connected, opening e preserves k_xi and the open/closed weight ratio is p/(1-p). Otherwise opening e decreases k_xi by one and the ratio is p/(q(1-p)). Converting odds r to probability r/(1+r) gives the formulas.
remaining_gap: This finite-graph identity supplies no continuum convergence or SLE identification; a partial exploration must average the full conditional law over unrevealed connectivity.

statement: For any finite random-cluster graph, 0<p<1 and q>0, fusing two fixed vertex boundary classes u,v gives Z_xi_uv/Z_xi=1/q+(1-1/q)P_q(u connected to v modulo xi). Restricted partition sums over a predictable adaptive exploration history satisfy the identical conditional formula; for q!=1, (q R_n-1)/(q-1) is the bounded Doob martingale of the fixed connectivity event.
assumptions: exactly two fixed vertex classes are fused
same p and q in both sums
same exploration-history restriction in both sums
adaptive edge queries depend only on revealed history
proof: The cluster count decreases by zero on connected configurations and by one otherwise. Divide the two restricted weight sums and use the conditional expectation of the one fixed event; then apply the tower property.
remaining_gap: No convergence of these conditional probabilities to any conformal boundary profile is established; arbitrary arc fusions do not obey the one-cluster decrement.

statement: For a fixed finite graph, fixed p in (0,1), and each fixed predictable exploration-history atom, P_1(u connected to v | F_n)=1+partial_q[Z_n^{uv}(q)/Z_n(q)] evaluated at q=1.
assumptions: same history atom and pair u,v in numerator and denominator
proof: Differentiate R_n(q)=q^-1+(1-q^-1)P_q(A|F_n) at q=1. The derivative of P_q is multiplied by zero there, leaving R_n'(1)=-1+P_1(A|F_n). Finite restricted partition sums are analytic at q=1.
remaining_gap: Mesh-uniform derivative control and random-slit convergence are unproved; this is not differentiation of expectations under a fixed law.

statement: Let W be a continuous adapted chordal Loewner driver with W0=0 in a usual filtration. On the common unswallowed interval for 0<x1<x2<y, set Ui=(g_t(xi)-W)/(g_t(y)-W). For fixed kappa>0 let H_kappa(u)=integral_{1/2}^u v^(-4/kappa)(1-v)^(8/kappa-2)dv. If both H_kappa(Ui) are continuous local martingales in that filtration, W is a continuous local martingale with d<W>=kappa dt there. For this assumption on every triple n,n+1,n+2, the conclusion holds globally and W/sqrt(kappa) is Brownian motion.
assumptions: two distinct ratios share the same outer point
both profile processes are continuous local martingales
proof: Invert H on compact subintervals to recover U1 as a semimartingale, then W=(g(x1)-U1*g(y))/(1-U1). Ito and H's logarithmic derivative give Y dA+(2/kappa)(1+1/Ui)(dV-kappa dt)=0 for i=1,2. Subtract and invert the nonzero coefficient to force dV=kappa dt and dA=0. Localize; global exhaustion requires all stated triples.
remaining_gap: The two FK conditional observables and their locally uniform, filtration-compatible conformal profile convergence have not been proved.

statement: A single H_kappa((g_t(x)-W)/(g_t(y)-W)) local martingale does not identify the variance of an arbitrary continuous Loewner driver: for any nu>0 unequal to kappa there exists a locally stopped driver with bracket nu dt and that martingale property.
counterexample: Solve dW=sqrt(nu)dB-2(nu-kappa)(1+1/U)/(kappa Y)dt together with the two Loewner point ODEs until exiting a compact region. The coefficients are smooth there, and the drift cancels the exact Ito finite-variation expression for H_kappa(U); the bracket stays nu dt.
remaining_gap: No FK realization is asserted; the example refutes only a one-observable abstract driver-identification inference.
